newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids lower as MGE falls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids lower as MGE falls.

text.p: Dark Northern Spring wheat cash bids were weaker on Friday as MGE futures continued to slide, and movement was generally slow although high protein wheat activity was strong, several cash brokers said.

"We're seeing more and more of the high-pro coming out," a Minnesota dealer said, referring to 14 and 15 percent protein wheat. He said several locations had been offering premiums for milling quality high protein wheat.
In Montana, forecasts called for snow over the weekend which should push winter wheat crops into dormancy, one Montana dealer noted.
"We're all done with (spring wheat) harvest and we're probably at least 80 to 90 percent seeded (winter wheat), so we're looking forward to the cold," the dealer said.

Farmer selling remained slow as producers held out for higher prices. Several brokers noted MGE December spring wheat futures were trading at $4.10-1/4 per bushel on Friday, down more than $2.00 per bushel since May.
Farmers were not likely to sell much wheat until prices rebounded to $5.00 per bushel, dealers speculated.
